consensus_summary: Settled Christian consensus takes 'fear of the LORD' primarily as reverent awe, worshipful respect and humble submission that is the beginning of wisdom/knowledge and produces obedience, covenant loyalty and hatred/turning from evil, rather than mere servile terror (while still allowing a residual element of trembling before holiness/judgment).
book_summary: Reverent awe expressed as keeping the commandments and departing from evil.
consensus_core_identification: reverent awe (not terror) that founds wisdom and is realized in obedience plus avoidance of evil
book_core_identification: reverent awe expressed as keeping the commandments and departing from evil
boundary_disagreement: None material; book’s behavioral focus is already an explicit consequence or near-synonym within the consensus primary sense.
rationale: Minimum cores are identical: both center on reverent awe (explicitly distinguished from pure dread) whose concrete form is commandment-keeping and departure from evil. Consensus primary statements and supporting texts (Prov 8:13; Job 28:28; Eccl 12:13; Deut 10:12) already treat those actions as the natural expression of the same awe; the book’s brevity therefore adds no new referent, excludes no consensus cases, and introduces no contradiction.
strongest_objection: The book’s silence on the ‘beginning of wisdom/knowledge’ motif (the single most-cited consensus emphasis) could be read as a quiet narrowing away from the noetic dimension.
